video_goal: Demonstrate how to properly sharpen a wooden pencil and empty the shavings tray using a Bostitch Personal Electric Pencil Sharpener.
required_subjects_and_props: Bostitch Personal Electric Pencil Sharpener, dull wooden pencil, desk surface, small wastebasket

outline_steps.visual_action: A Bostitch Personal Electric Pencil Sharpener sits on a flat wooden desk, with the camera panning slightly to highlight the Bostitch logo on the front.
A hand enters the frame holding a yellow wooden pencil, rotating it slowly to display the broken, flat graphite tip.
The hand guides the dull pencil downward toward the circular insertion hole on the top of the Bostitch sharpener.
The hand pushes the pencil down into the insertion hole until it stops, keeping a firm grip on the pencil shaft.
The sharpener vibrates slightly on the desk as the hand holds the pencil steady, preventing the pencil from spinning.
Wood and graphite shavings rapidly fall and accumulate inside the front translucent shavings tray of the sharpener.
The hand pulls the pencil straight up and completely out of the sharpener's top insertion hole.
The hand rotates the pencil between the thumb and index finger, displaying a sharp, pointed graphite tip.
The hand places the sharpened pencil down on the desk beside the sharpener.
The thumb and index finger pinch the textured side grips of the translucent shavings tray on the front of the sharpener.
The hand pulls the translucent shavings tray straight out from the sharpener body, exposing a pile of fresh wood shavings inside.
The hand moves the tray over a small wastebasket and tilts it upside down, causing the shavings to fall out.
The hand aligns the empty translucent tray with the front opening of the Bostitch sharpener and pushes it in until it sits flush.
